result:
The apartment was never truly silent. There was always the hum of the refrigerator, the distant wail of a siren, the muffled thump of a neighbor's bass. But this evening, as the rain began to fall, a different kind of quiet settled in. It wasn't an absence of sound, but a presence of a different texture. The drops against the windowpane were a soft, steady percussion, a natural metronome for my thoughts.

I sat on the floor, a mug of tea warming my hands, and let the noise of the day drain out of me. The frantic emails, the endless scroll, the constant pinging of notifications—all of it faded into a whisper. In that space, I could finally hear myself think. Not the anxious, looping thoughts of the day, but a deeper, slower current. This silence felt like a room I had forgotten I owned. A room I rarely visited, but one that was always waiting, dusty but intact. It held my daydreams, my half-remembered conversations, my unanswered questions. I wasn't running from the world; I was simply taking a breath before re-entering it.

As the rain softened, the traffic sounds returned, and the spell was broken. But the quiet had done its work. It had reminded me that beneath the frantic surface, there is a place that is always calm, always still. I just have to remember to find it.
